mechanics.executable_reminder: {Cost}: Transform this permanent. Attach this permanent to target creature you control without a Steed enchantment attached to it. Activate only as a sorcery.

rule_text.name: 702.261a
rule_text.rule: Ride is an activated ability of some double-faced cards. “Ride [cost]” means “[cost]: Transform this creature and attach it to target creature you control that doesn't have a Steed enchantment attached to it. As long as this card remains attached to a permanent, you may pay [cost] any time you could cast a sorcery to unattach it from that permanent. Ride only as a sorcery.”

rule_text.name: 702.261b
rule_text.rule: If a Steed is on the battlefield not attached to a permanent, it transforms rather than being put into its owner's graveyard if able. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)

rule_text.name: 702.261c
rule_text.rule: The creature a Steed card enchants may be referred to as its “rider”. Effects that refer to a Steed's rider are identical to those that would refer to enchanted creature.

rule_text.name: 702.261d
rule_text.rule: One card (Bonescourge Kazadrak) allows its ride ability to be activated from its owner's graveyard. If this is done, the card will be put onto the battlefield transformed rather than transforming the card.

rule_text.name: 702.261e
rule_text.rule: One card (The Scourgebone Pact) states that its rider "can't dismount". This means a player can't pay [cost] to unattach the Steed from the creature it is attached to. The Steed will still transform back to its front face if it is unattached somehow, such as its rider leaving the battlefield.
